title: Publishing and maintaining a static website
learningObjectives: Complete publishing and maintaining a static website using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: Publishing a static site includes validating the build, configuring hosting and HTTPS, checking routes and assets, and running post-deployment smoke tests. Maintenance includes monitoring, dependency updates, content review, backups where needed, and a rollback or forward-fix process.
understand.whyItMatters: A published site continues to need care. Caching and deployment changes can break previously working routes, and updates should be traceable to known commits.
understand.analogy: Publishing opens the site to visitors; maintenance keeps the doors, signs, and services working afterward.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The list describes recurring maintenance tasks. The schedule should match the project's risk and release cadence.

practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
